Vivek —

Thanks. High-level updates from product:

1) Model-routing UI (Priority A) — GREEN. UX sign-off complete; backend contract stable. No customer-facing change.

2) Dedicated autoscaling policies (Priority A) — YELLOW. Work is functionally complete but blocked by canary instability (see Markus' note). Impact: stretches Dedicated rollouts by 2 weeks if we can’t fix canary.

3) VPC/private control-plane (Priority B) — GREEN. Security review done; scheduling rollout in April.

4) Quantization profile option (Priority A) — RED (decision needed). We still need to pick a default quant target (int8 vs int4) for the GA build. Product needs a recommendation from Eng on quality tradeoffs and fallback behavior.

Owners: I'll own the product-side mitigation for quantization (work with Markus). Attached is a quick CSV with feature-level status & owners.

Laura

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-28 14:20 -0800
Subject: Re: Quarterly briefing prep — roadmap health + asks (please review by EOD Mon)

Quick engineering flags — mostly focused on Dedicated/autoscaling and quantization tradeoffs.

1) Canary instability: During the last round of canary tests (INF-412) we observed a tail-latency regression under mixed workload (multi-tenant inference + embeddings) tied to our new batching path. Repro steps included a 60-minute soak; root cause appears to be suboptimal KV cache eviction under the new allocator.
   - Impact: latency SLOs violated for 95th/99th in canary; must not hit GA without mitigation.
   - Short-term mitigation: revert to previous KV eviction policy and reduce batch-size defaults for Dedicated pools.
   - Owner: Markus + Eng infra. ETA for mitigation patch: 4 business days after approval to push revert.

2) CUDA driver: The vendor has not certified our newest CUDA build on the dedicated GPU fleet image. This blocks quantized int4 kernels on the Dedicated infra for some customers.
   - Impact: int4 quantization path may need to be disabled for Dedicated GA, which increases token-costs per inference for those customers.
   - Contingency: expose a 'quantization-mode' toggle per pool and ship with int8 default for Dedicated until driver cert completes.

3) Quantization QA: we need a formal prompt set and eval for int4 vs int8 to quantify quality delta before product picks a default. Can we prioritize a small labeled eval set (15–20 prompts/customer) for Atlas Health (Emily Park) since they are sensitive to hallucination risk?

Attaching canary test logs for context.

-Markus

Heading into release planning — timeline notes: 

- Original GA target: 2027-03-14 for Dedicated rollout to pilot customers. Given the canary instability and driver uncertainty, propose moving GA by two weeks to 2027-03-28 for a controlled, staged rollout. This buys Eng a full week for mitigation + 1 week for extended canary.
- Customer-facing plan: staged rollout — pilot group (Atlas Health, EdgeOps) on 3/28, broader customers on 4/11.
- If we accept moving the date, we should notify Sales & CS by EOD tomorrow to adjust communications and renewal offers.

I've attached an updated timeline with milestones and dependencies. Owners are called out on the sheet.

Tessa

Couple of finance/ops notes that will shape our QBR narrative: 

- Cost impact: If int4 is disabled on Dedicated (per Markus' note) we estimate a +18–25% per-token cost for affected customers. Need a comms plan with pricing options or credits for pilot customers.
- SLA cues: the autoscaling tail-latency risk means we should avoid promising tighter latency SLAs for Dedicated GA. Propose we keep current SLA language and add an "improvement roadmap" in the QBR slides rather than change contractual terms mid-quarter.
- Action: Sales & Finance alignment call to evaluate marking for renewals impacted by the date shift. I can own that sync — suggest Tue 3/2 10am PT if that works.

Attaching a short SLO impact summary.

-Stephanie

Subject: Consolidated QBR inputs & action tracker (please ack)

Thanks for the rapid responses — good level of detail. Below is a consolidated view and direct action items so we can close the QBR doc by EOD tomorrow.

Summary bullets for slides: 
- Roadmap health: Mostly green for core UX and private control plane; Dedicated autoscaling is yellow due to canary tail-latency regression. Quantization default undecided (red) pending eval.
- Timeline: Recommend shifting GA from 2027-03-14 to 2027-03-28 for a staged pilot-first rollout (Atlas Health, EdgeOps).
- Risks: (1) Canary tail-latency (owner: Markus; ETA patch: 4 business days after revert approval), (2) CUDA driver certification (owner: Eng infra; contingency: int8 default + per-pool quant toggle), (3) Cost delta if int4 not available (+18–25% token cost — owner: Stephanie).

Action items (owners + deadlines):
1) Approve short-term revert to previous KV eviction policy so Markus can push the mitigation patch (Owner: Vivek to approve; Due: 2027-03-01 EOD).
2) Build a 20-prompt eval set for Atlas Health to compare int4 vs int8 quality (Owner: Markus + Laura; Due: 2027-03-04).
3) Notify Sales/CS and prepare customer comms for staged rollout (Owner: Tessa + Stephanie; Due: 2027-03-02).
4) Update QBR one-pager and slide deck with the timeline shift and risk notes (Owner: Laura; Due: 2027-03-01 noon).
5) Finance/Sales sync re: credits/pricing (Owner: Stephanie; Meeting scheduled: 2027-03-02 10:00 PT).

Emily — cc'ing you because Atlas Health is part of the pilot group. If you have any urgent constraints on testing or timeline, please call them out here.

Please ack and call out any corrections. I'll approve the revert once I have confirmation from Eng that rollback is low-risk. After approvals I'll update the QBR doc and send to GTM.

-Vivek
